title: Invertibility of a single lifted adjacent comparison
statement: Let X be Noetherian, J an ideal sheaf, and j_n : T_n → X closed immersions with kernel J^(n+1), with i_n ≫ j_(n+1) = j_n and supplied tensor-pullback adjunctions [lem-weil-pbc-thickening-system-pushforward-functor]. Let H be a coherent formal module [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. For one n, let F on T_n and G on T_(n+1) be coherent modules with isomorphisms eF : j_(n,*)F ≅ H_n and eG : j_(n+1,*)G ≅ H_(n+1). If u : G → i_(n,*)F has pushforward agreeing, after the canonical pushforward-composition comparison and eF, with eG followed by the adjacent H transition, then the adjoint map i_n^*G → F is invertible. No coherent thickening system or inverse-system isomorphism is asserted.

proof.text: Use the closedness of j_n = i_n followed by j_(n+1) to infer closedness of i_n. The identities comap_map_of_isClosedImmersion, map_ker, and comap_pow identify its kernel with (J.comap j_(n+1))^(n+1). The source T_(n+1) is locally Noetherian, so coherence of G implies quasi-coherence.

Apply closedImmersion_power_quotient to i_n with the supplied adjunction ai_n and G. Compose with the quotient comparison of closedImmersion_pushforward_idealPowers along j_(n+1) and the canonical composition comparison to obtain d: (j_(n+1,*)G)/J^(n+1) ≅ j_(n,*)i_n^*G. The projection followed by d.hom is pushforward of ai_n.unit at G followed by the composition comparison.

Transport quotients along eG using formalModuleQuotientMap and its identity/composition laws, giving an isomorphism e. Obtain the adjacent quotient isomorphism a from H.property.2.2 n. For f adjoint to u, the adjunction identity, naturality of the pushforward-composition comparison, and hu imply d.hom followed by j_(n,*)f and eF.hom equals e.hom followed by a.hom: precompose by the epimorphic quotient projection and use its defining equations. Thus j_(n,*)f = d.inv followed by e.hom, a.hom, eF.inv, an isomorphism.
Use closedImmersion_pushforward_fullyFaithful to equip j_(n,*) with Full and Faithful instances, then reflect the isomorphism of its image to prove IsIso f.
